note.text:
A clause is a group of words with a subject and a verb.
• A main clause makes sense on its own: The boy reported the bully.
• A subordinate clause does not make sense alone; it begins with a subordinator such as because, when, if, although, while, since, after, before, until: … because he was afraid.
A complex sentence = main clause + subordinate clause: The boy reported the bully because he was afraid.
When the subordinate clause comes first, put a comma after it: Although he was afraid, he reported the bully.

worked_example.problem: Find the main clause: “When the bell rang, the fight stopped.”
steps: “When the bell rang” begins with when: it does not make sense alone.
“the fight stopped” makes sense alone: it is the main clause.

cards.idea: A main clause makes sense on its own.
A subordinate clause begins with because, when, if, although …
Join two sentences with a subordinator.

questions.prompt: Which is the main clause in: “{X.q}”?

pick.s: He was punished ___ he bullied a younger boy.
e: The second clause gives the reason: because.

pick.s: ___ you see drugs in school, report it.
e: It is a condition, not a contrast.

pick.s: ___ he was afraid, he told the truth.
e: Afraid but brave: a contrast, although.
It is a fact, not a condition.

right.text: A main clause makes sense on its own.
“because he was afraid” is a subordinate clause.
A complex sentence has a main and a subordinate clause.
When the subordinate clause comes first, we use a comma.

wrong.text: “When the bell rang.” is a complete sentence.
wrong.explain: It is a subordinate clause; it needs a main clause.

wrong.text: A subordinate clause always begins with “and”.
wrong.explain: It begins with a subordinator: because, when, if, although …

wrong.text: A main clause cannot have a verb.
wrong.explain: Every clause has a subject and a verb.
